messages:
Maria L: quick convo — linked a short proposal (https://tiny.redwood/proposals/telemetry-sampling). main Q: should we lean into head sampling at the OTEL collector to cut egress cost, or prefer tail sampling in the backend so we don't lose error context? thoughts?

Kai T: head sampling is easiest to get immediate savings (drop before exporters). downside: you can accidentally lose the few traces you actually need for debugging (errors/latency). head + deterministic key per-customer is usually good for quota fairness.

Sasha R: +1 on deterministic key. also want to stress: tail sampling preserves root/span relationships for errors. my recommended pattern: global low-rate head sampling to reduce noise, then run a tail-sampling pass for error/slow traces + reservoir for rare routes. preserves high-value traces while cutting volume.

Ben P: for deterministic sampling we do something like `hash(customer_id || route) % 100 < N` so each customer gets consistent fraction. keeps signal stable across restarts.

Maria L: how do we do dynamic per-route / per-tier adjustments? e.g., enterprise customers get higher sample budget, noisy public routes get lower. can we autoscale sample rate by observed QPS or cost budget?

emma (Product): from console UX POV we want: per-route slider + tier overrides, preview estimated monthly telemetry cost delta, and a canary toggle (dry-run) before enforce. non-engineering teams should be able to see impact.

Sasha R: prototype config for collector + tail service (rough):
```yaml
policies:
  - name: global-head
    type: probabilistic
    rate: 0.02
  - name: preserve-errors
    type: tail
    eval: 'status_code >= 500 or latency_ms > 2000'
  - name: route-overrides
    type: dynamic
    selector: route
    algorithm: qps_based
    min_rate: 0.001
    max_rate: 0.2
```
This lets us do cheap early filtering and still run a richer tail pass for important traces.

Maria L: good. also: cardinality risk — many span attributes (user_email, prompt_hash, model_variant) will explode downstream indexes. propose attribute whitelist & deterministic hashing for high-cardinality fields, e.g. `prompt_hash = sha256(prompt)[:8]` only.

Kai T: agree on whitelist. also recommend adding a `sample_reason` and `sample_key` tag to exported spans so we can reconstruct how a span survived sampling and tie back to budgets. if we head-drop we should emit a tiny metric with dropped counts per-route/customer.

observability-bot: alert — "span_drop_rate" for route "/v1/generate" > 0.5 over 5m (svc=hosted-api)

Ben P: metrics to add: `spans_ingested`, `spans_exported`, `span_drop_rate`, `sampled_rate_by_route`, `preserved_errors_count`, and `telemetry_bytes_exported`. these should feed a console chart and an infra billing estimate.

Sasha R: implementation notes: tail sampling requires buffering (time window) — we should be careful about memory/backpressure. reservoir of 10k traces per-second across all routes might be fine initially; we can move heavy tail evaluation to a separate service with async pulls from collector.

Maria L: good discussion. next steps: Sasha will spike collector policy + reservoir prototype (owner: Sasha R). Ben will wire the basic metrics + a mock console chart (owner: Ben P). I (Maria) will work with @emma to draft the console UX for route sliders and a canary/dry-run flow. target: prototype + demo next Thu. :thumbsup:

Kai T: sounds good — I'll add deterministic sampling helper lib and a small test harness.

emma (Product): thanks everyone — we'll want a quick writeup for GTM once prototype shows savings.

Maria L: tagging this as FYI for eng-platform and eng-sre. dropping the design doc link again: https://tiny.redwood/proposals/telemetry-sampling
